comparison: Perfect agreement on SGC overrepresentation in behaviorally labeled neurons (C35-C37, C69, C108). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with adequate statistical analysis and sample sizes. Peer reviewers note consistency with previous observations and describe this as 'solid evidence.'

Complete agreement on intrinsic physiological differences (C3, C42, C44-C47, C64, C75-C76). Both evaluations find the electrophysiological evidence SUPPORTED, particularly the finding that labeled SGCs show reduced adaptation compared to unlabeled SGCs. Peer reviewers accept this explains preferential SGC recruitment.

Agreement on basic electrophysiological characterization of GCs (C38-C41, C43, C73). Both evaluations find these control measurements SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these negative findings strengthen specificity of SGC adaptation results; peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting differences between SGCs and GCs regardless of labeling.

Significant disagreement on lack of recurrent excitation between labeled neurons (C5, C48, C67, C87). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with adequate sample size and controls. Peer Reviewer 2 rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 32 pairs is sufficient and whether preparation quality affects connectivity detection, though acknowledges some synaptic connections are preserved.

Disagreement on minimal lateral inhibition findings (C6, C49-C51, C68, C92-C93, C96, C98-C99). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on extensive paired recordings (104 total) and controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with concerns about connectivity rates compared to other studies and slice preparation limitations, though acknowledge the descriptive findings.

Agreement on positive control experiments (C52, C94-C95, C97). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this validates slice preparation can support lateral inhibition. Peer Reviewer 2 specifically acknowledges this addresses concerns about preparation quality by demonstrating preserved synaptic connections.

Complete agreement on enhanced sEPSC frequency and amplitude in labeled neurons (C7, C55-C58, C65, C88). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and sample sizes. Peer reviewers list this as a strength of the study without challenge.

Strong agreement on temporal correlation of excitatory inputs (C8, C59-C63, C66, C89-C90). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2 calls this 'the most convincing finding' and notes additional analyses strengthen the conclusion. All reviewers accept the cross-correlation analysis and ROC discrimination results.

Agreement on TTX validation experiment (C53-C54). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this justifies correlation analyses. Peer Reviewer 2 initially raised concerns about using spontaneous EPSCs but acknowledges this control experiment addresses those concerns.

Agreement on behavioral labeling and reactivation experiments (C30-C34, C104). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes nested statistics and reactivation validation. Peer Reviewer 3 notes validation across two paradigms as a strength. Partial overlap with R11 concerns about reactivation rates.

Partial overlap on methodological considerations (C100-C103). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, viewing these as appropriate experimental troubleshooting. Peer reviewers also accept the approach (R10) but express some concerns about timing and reactivation rates that connect to R11 evaluation.

Disagreement on reactivation rate implications (C105-C107). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, viewing low reactivation as consistent with literature and appropriately discussed as limitation. Peer Reviewer 2 rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 7% reactivation rate undermines meaningfulness of the labeled ensemble and noting the week-long delay as a major caveat.

Disagreement on integrative mechanistic conclusions (C71, C110). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as well-integrated synthesis of multiple experimental findings. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with concerns that data are 'descriptive and based on correlation rather than causation' and that slice physiology limitations affect mechanistic interpretations, though editor acknowledges 'solid evidence' for recruitment mechanisms.

OpenEval identifies speculative claims (C70, C77, C79, C80, C82) as UNCERTAIN, noting they lack direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these speculative interpretations as a separate category, though peer concerns about causation vs. correlation (R12) relate to similar interpretive issues.
